xrefcode.com / docs / cli / live-profile

$ xref live profile

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page
  1. Usage
  2. Arguments and options
  3. Examples
  4. Record two seconds
  5. Daemons and processes that come and go
  6. Limits
  7. Provenance

Sample where a running process spends its CPU time and save a bounded recording (.xprof) that the profile commands read: hot functions, blocks and instructions, with call chains unwound from .eh_frame (--callers dwarf, the default). Recording can be limited to a function (--within) or to windows opened by a uprobe trigger.

Usage

xref live profile [OPTIONS]

Arguments and options

Options

--pid <PID>
Target process ID; with --comm or --argv-match it may be left out to wait for the first match.
--follow-children
Also sample every process a sampled process forks (fork without exec), as it starts [alias: --follow-fork].
--comm <COMM>
Also sample processes of the same executable with this name (/proc/PID/comm) as they start.
--argv-match <ARGV_MATCH>
Also sample processes of the same executable whose command line contains this text.
--duration <DURATION>
Capture duration, e.g. 10s or 200ms.
default 10s
--duration-ms <DURATION_MS>
Capture duration in milliseconds.
--freq <FREQ>
Requested samples per second per thread; defaults to 4000 [alias: --hz].
--period <PERIOD>
Hardware events per sample instead of a frequency.
--event <EVENT>
Hardware event that drives sampling [possible values: cycles, instructions, cache-misses, branch-misses].
default cycles
--tid <TIDS>
Sample only this thread ID (repeatable); all threads by default.
--callers <CALLERS>
How call chains are recorded: DWARF stack copies unwound with .eh_frame, LBR, frame pointers, or none [alias: --callgraph] [possible values: dwarf, lbr, fp, none].
default dwarf
--within <WITHIN>
Report only samples whose call chain includes this function or address (repeatable).
--trigger-probe <TRIGGER_PROBE>
Code address whose uprobe hits open recording windows; without it the whole duration is recorded.
--window <WINDOW>
Length of each trigger window, e.g. 200ms (the default).
--window-ms <WINDOW_MS>
Length of each trigger window in milliseconds.
--max-windows <MAX_WINDOWS>
Record up to this many separate post-trigger windows.
--trigger-fetch <TRIGGER_FETCH>
Named tracefs fetch, e.g. op=+40(%sp):u64, for trigger filtering.
--trigger-filter <TRIGGER_FILTER>
Numeric predicate over a named trigger fetch.
--json
Print the capture statistics and the report as JSON.
--folded <FOLDED>
Also write folded stacks (flame-graph input) to this new file.
--out <OUT>
Keep the .xprof recording at this new path; without it a temporary recording is deleted after the report.
--max-samples <MAX_SAMPLES>
Stop recording after this many samples.
default 10000000
--stack-bytes <STACK_BYTES>
User stack bytes copied with each sample for DWARF unwinding.
default 2048
--include-kernel
Include kernel-mode samples; requires suitable perf permissions.

Examples

The target is ripgrep 14.1.1 (rg) filtering an endless input stream, as on live maps. PIDs and runtime addresses belong to that run.

Record two seconds

Command
$ xref -b rg live profile --pid 3669251 --duration 2s --out rg.xprof
Output
capture: 2000 ms, observer thread CPU: 34 ms (excludes target and interrupt-context overhead)
7347 samples, 0 lost, 0 dropped; partial=true
target mapping: /srv/xref-docs/rg
  30.43% self   30.43% total       2236 [kernel]:unknown
  17.35% self   26.09% total       1275 target:fn_430060
  12.48% self   15.56% total        917 target:fn_10b0c0
  10.04% self   42.77% total        738 target:fn_de140
   4.57% self   32.72% total        336 target:fn_138ef0
   3.85% self   46.62% total        283 target:fn_fb4b0
   3.66% self    3.66% total        269 target:fn_4307b0
   2.49% self    2.49% total        183 target:unknown
   2.26% self    2.26% total        166 target:fn_408bf0
   2.22% self    2.22% total        163 target:fn_4752a0
   2.18% self   66.68% total        160 target:fn_fc020
   2.06% self    2.06% total        151 target:fn_13af50
   1.70% self    5.09% total        125 target:fn_4302b0

   0.59% self    3.08% total         43 target:fn_319d40
Output cut here: lines 1–20 of 39 shown.

The summary printed after the capture is the same report as profile report. Samples are never attributed to the target when they fall outside it. A shared library whose file on disk is verified to be the one mapped in the process is symbolized as its own module; a library that cannot be verified (changed or missing file) or has no symbols, and kernel samples, stay unknown frames of their module, as [kernel]:unknown does here.

Daemons and processes that come and go

--follow-children also samples every process that a sampled process forks without exec, such as a daemon started by fork, setsid and a second fork. xref learns of a fork from the parent's perf fork record and, as a fallback, from /proc. It accepts a process whose parent, process group or session belongs to the target's family, so a daemon whose parent already exited is still found.

--comm NAME and --argv-match TEXT add processes whose name or command line matches, as they start. A benchmark that starts a new process every round is profiled with one command. Without --pid, xref waits for the first match. Every added process must run the same executable file (same device and inode) as the target; others are refused and counted. A process that execs another program leaves the profile. Each process keeps its own address layout, so separately started instances are attributed correctly.

Command
# The session daemon, a grandchild of the command that starts it:
sudo xref -b tako-session live profile --pid "$(pgrep -n tako)" --follow-children --duration 12s
# Every instance a benchmark starts during the window:
sudo xref -b tako-session live profile --comm tako-session --duration 12s --out bench.xprof

A process is sampled from when xref attaches to it: xref drains fork records every 2 ms and scans /proc every 25 ms, so the first milliseconds of a short-lived process can be missed. These options cannot be combined with --tid or a trigger.

Limits

  • Needs perf access to the process: with kernel.perf_event_paranoid 1 (the setting of the recording host) a user may profile their own processes; kernel samples need --include-kernel and a setting that allows them.
  • --out does not overwrite an existing file.
  • Chains whose unwinding stops (missing CFI, code outside the binary) are counted in the warning: lines rather than guessed.

Provenance

Recorded with xref 0.6.0 (the remapped release build of commit 1171b426, made by scripts/package-release.sh before the tag) on Linux x86-64, on rg = ripgrep 14.1.1 (official stripped release). Live examples ran against one ripgrep process filtering an endless input stream; commands shown with sudo ran as root. Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
